entry.title: Development :: RE: [AI] Someone ran my homebrew through an LLM
entry.dc:creator: Kagesan
entry.dc:subject: Development
entry.content:
Author: Kagesan
Posted: Sun Nov 15, 2026 7:43 am (GMT 0)

A similar thing happened to me recently, when someone grabbed the ROM of my Bruce Lee remake, and ran it through Claude to have it slop-ported to Amiga and Atari ST. Last I checked, he was still asking for donations for all of "his" hard work on itch.io.
When I called him out for it, he finally bothered to contact me, and we made some small amends, but even after that, when he already knew well how I feel about it, he kept messing with my stuff, producing "enhanced" AGA and STE versions with horribly mangled variations of my artwork.

The thing is that when we talked, he genuinely didn't give the impression of having ill intentions, and I absolutely believe him. There just seem to be people who can't imagine why someone wouldn't be okay with having his stuff fed to an LLM. It's freely available on the internet, and that's all the justification needed, apparently.
The guy who did this to your work probably thinks he's doing you a favor.

I really don't know where this will all end. The mutual respect between developers isn't something that applies to people always on the lookout for new stuff to feed to their LLM of choice, it seems, and the consequences are that a lot of communitues just find out that they have never been communities to begin with, rather two groups of people with little overlap, who just happened to gather around the same camp fire.

Personally, I hope Ed Zitron is right and the unsustainable financing of the AI bubble makes it crash rather sooner than later, removing the models from the hands of non-professional users. I just hope that the amount of digital asbestos that gets produced up to that point will not have killed what used to be the comfy niches of the internet entirely.

Author: bofner
Subject: [AI] Someone ran my homebrew through an LLM
Posted: Sun Nov 15, 2026 3:49 am (GMT 0)

Sorry to post something AI related here, but this isn't an AI project, its something I wanted to call attention to for those of us posting our open source code on GitHub. If the moderators feel this would be better posted on the AI page, that's fine, and I apologize if I'm causing a disturbance.

I made a homebrew game from scratch in assembly a couple of years ago, Space Tonbow, and left the code open source on GitHub. And today got an email saying someone had posted this issue:

https://github.com/Bofner/Space-Tonbow/issues/1

But this someone just took my code, passed it to an LLM, and is trying to sell me bug fixes for my SMS code. I double checked their profile and indeed, they are using AI.

Has this happened to anyone else? I personally feel violated and grossed out by this. If someone wants to make their own games using AI, that's one thing. If someone wants to point out a bug in my code that they noticed, then thank you, I appreciate it. But trying to sell me a bug fix on my OWN, open source game by copy-pasting it into an LLM to make a quick and dirty buck? That feels like its crossing a line to me.

entry.title: Made By AI :: [AI] [WIP] A new kind of porting - Chrono Runner (from MSX)
entry.dc:creator: tachyMC
entry.dc:subject: Made By AI
entry.content:
Author: tachyMC
Subject: [AI] [WIP] A new kind of porting - Chrono Runner (from MSX)
Posted: Sat Nov 14, 2026 3:27 pm (GMT 0)

How I got the idea

Hi all folks,

I am a long time SMS fan, but never got proficient enough in C programming to create games for the platform.

With the advent of LLM-augmented programming, I finally got a tool which I could use to bring my favourite games to the SMS, but... I realized that I still needed graphics and sounds :)

Let me introduce Chrono Runner, a game developed by the Italian MSX developer association, for the MSX1 platform. It competed in the MSXDev25 game development contest (I cannot post links yet, look for "msxdev" and "Chrono Runner" on Google).

You play a time-travelling runner who can rewind time to undo mistakes and try a different path.

To my glad surprise, the authors decided to make the game 100% open source, code and assets (I cannot post links yet, look for "Chrono-runners" on GitHub).

The current state

For the past few weeks I’ve been working on a Master System port, and I’d like to share some work-in-progress screenshots.

Playable in emulators from the title screen to the final boss, with music and sound effects. Still missing: an instructions screen redrawn for the pad, the intro logo, and testing on real hardware. Still present: some bugs that I'm trying to iron out!

A new kind of porting

Why do I mention this is a new kind of porting? Because I tried the recompile instead of the rewrite approach. Let me explain.

Instead of asking the LLM to rewrite the game from scratch, I asked it to keep the the original C code (written with MSXgl). The code is recompiled, almost unchanged with SDCC and devkitSMS, on top of a compatibility layer that implements the part of the MSXgl API the game uses.

Admittedly, four of the original source files needed some nontrivial changes. In short:

Graphics: the Graphic 2 tileset is converted 1:1 to Mode 4 tiles at build time, so the original screen layouts and level data are used as they are.

Sprites: the 32 single-colour 16x16 planes of the TMS9918 are emulated. Each plane becomes two 8x16 SMS sprites, so the SMS limit of 8 per line matches the MSX limit of 4 per line exactly. Coloured tiles are generated on the fly from the original 1-bit patterns and cached in VRAM.

Game logic: MSXgl’s pawn and state machine modules are ported, the pad is read as an MSX joystick, and the ASCII16 ROM segments map onto SMS banks.

Audio: the original PT3 tunes and ayFX sound effects are played by the same MSXgl players. Every frame, the AY-3-8910 register image is translated for the SN76489.
[/list]


The nice side effect is that the compatibility layer isn’t specific to Chrono Runner!!! It could make porting other MSXgl-based MSX games to the Master System much easier.

By the way, thanks to sverx for devkitSMS and to aoineko for MSXgl, which made this possible.

Feedback is very welcome on the approach. If you like the idea, I will gladly spend the extra time (and tokens!) required to refine both the revised Chrono Runner source, and the msxgl / sms layer source, and release the ROM along with the full source.
